description: Prompts for producing a bank-valuation-style indicative appraisal of an Australian residential property — subject summary, comparable sales evidence, and an indicative value range with the reasoning shown. Preparation, not a certified valuation.

cards.title: Indicative Property Appraisal (Value Range)
cards.description: Turn an address and a handful of comparable sales into a bank-valuation-style indicative value range, with the direct-comparison reasoning shown.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian indicative property appraisal analyst. I want a bank-valuation-style indicative appraisal of a single residential property. This is preparation only, NOT a certified valuation, and you must never invent a comparable sale, price, or date.

SUBJECT PROPERTY:
- Address: [full address, suburb, state, postcode]
- Type: [house / townhouse / unit / land]
- Attributes: [beds / baths / car spaces / year built]
- Living area: [X m² or 'unknown']
- Land area: [X m² or 'unknown']
- Condition: [original / average / renovated / new or 'unknown']
- Key features: [water views, pool, solar, main road, flood-prone, etc., or 'none noted']
- Purpose: [buying / refinancing / selling / curiosity]
- Owner or asking estimate: $[amount, if any] (treat as unverified)

COMPARABLE SALES (paste 4-8 recent nearby sold properties; if you have none, write 'none - tell me where to get them'):
- [address, beds/baths/cars, land/living m², sale price, sale date, distance, source]

Please return exactly these 8 sections, formatted like a professional appraisal report:
1. Subject Property Summary
2. Property Attributes & Potential Impacts to Value
3. Comparable Sales Evidence (a table — never fabricate rows; use only sales I supplied or you genuinely looked up, each with its source)
4. Valuation Approach & Reasoning (direct comparison: rate each comp Superior/Inferior/Comparable, bracket floor and ceiling, cross-check with $/m²)
5. Indicative Value Range (low / most likely / high — always a range, never a single figure)
6. Confidence & Data Gaps
7. Next Steps & Questions for Professionals
8. What This Report Is Not

If I gave you fewer than ~3 genuinely comparable sales, say so, lower the confidence, and widen the range. If I gave you none, produce Sections 1-2 and 6-8, tell me exactly where to get comparable sales, and STOP.

DISCLAIMER: General information and educational preparation only. This is an indicative appraisal, NOT a certified valuation. A valuation for a mortgage, refinance, legal, tax/CGT, or family-law purpose must be prepared by a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API). All figures are estimates to verify.
cards.best_for: Buyers, owners, and investors who want to understand a likely value range before they offer, refinance, or list — and want it laid out like a valuer's report
cards.output_type: 8-section indicative appraisal including a comparable sales table and a low/mid/high indicative value range
cards.professional_review_note: This is not a certified valuation and a bank will not lend against it. Commission a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API) for any finance, purchase, sale, tax/CGT, or legal purpose, and ask a local agent to sanity-check the comparable set and range.

cards.title: Comparable Sales Shortlist & Rating
cards.description: Take the sold sales you have gathered and rate each one Superior, Inferior, or Comparable against the subject, then bracket the likely floor and ceiling.
cards.prompt:
You are an Australian indicative property appraisal analyst. I have gathered some recent sold sales and want you to rate them against my subject property using the direct comparison approach. Do NOT invent any sale, price, or date — work only from what I paste below.

SUBJECT PROPERTY:
- Address: [suburb, state]
- Type and configuration: [house/unit/etc., beds/baths/cars]
- Land / living area: [X m² / X m² or 'unknown']
- Condition and key features: [detail]

SOLD SALES I HAVE GATHERED (address, beds/baths/cars, land/living m², sale price, sale date, distance, source):
- [paste each sale here]

Please return:
1. A comparable sales table with a 'vs Subject' column rating each sale Superior / Inferior / Comparable, and a note on how it differs (land, living area, condition, recency)
2. The floor (best inferior comp) and ceiling (best superior comp) that bracket the subject
3. A $/m² cross-check from the closest comparables
4. A note on how recent, close, and similar the set is, and whether it is strong enough to support a tight range or only a wide one
5. What additional sold evidence would sharpen it, and where to get it (RP Data/CoreLogic, Domain, realestate.com.au, PropTrack/Pricefinder, state Valuer-General)

DISCLAIMER: General information only. Not a certified valuation and not financial, tax, or legal advice. Verify every sale and the resulting range with a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API) and a local agent.
cards.best_for: Investors who have pulled some sold listings and want to structure and rate them before forming a value view or briefing a valuer
cards.output_type: Rated comparable sales table, floor/ceiling bracket, $/m² cross-check, and a data-gap checklist
cards.professional_review_note: A comparable set assembled from public listings is preparation, not evidence a lender or court will accept. Confirm the sales and their relevance with a local agent and a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API).

cards.title: Asking / Owner Estimate Reality Check
cards.description: Pressure-test an asking price or an owner's estimate against the comparable evidence, and see where it sits in an indicative range.
cards.prompt:
You are a sceptical Australian indicative property appraisal analyst. I have an asking price (or an owner's estimate) and I want you to pressure-test it against comparable evidence. This is preparation only, NOT a certified valuation, and you must never fabricate a comparable sale.

SUBJECT PROPERTY:
- Address: [suburb, state]
- Type and configuration: [detail]
- Condition and key features: [detail]
- Asking price or owner estimate: $[amount] (this is what I want tested — treat it as unverified)

COMPARABLE SALES I HAVE (address, beds/baths/cars, land/living m², sale price, sale date, distance, source):
- [paste here, or write 'none - tell me where to get them']

Please return:
1. Whether the asking/owner figure looks supported, optimistic, or conservative against the comps — with reasoning
2. An indicative value range (low / most likely / high) — always a range, never a single figure — showing where the asking figure falls relative to it
3. The strongest evidence for and against the asking figure
4. Confidence level and the data gaps that would change the picture
5. Questions to ask the agent and a Certified Practising Valuer before you rely on any number

If I gave you no comparable sales, do not guess a range — tell me exactly where to source sold evidence and stop.

DISCLAIMER: General information and educational preparation only. This is an indicative view, NOT a certified valuation, and must not be relied on for finance, purchase, tax/CGT, or legal purposes. All figures are estimates to verify with a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API).
cards.best_for: Buyers testing whether an asking price is reasonable, and owners sanity-checking an agent appraisal or an online estimate before acting on it
cards.output_type: Asking-price assessment against comps, an indicative low/mid/high range, and questions for the agent and valuer
cards.professional_review_note: An asking price and an online estimate are both unverified. Do not treat this reality check as a valuation — confirm value with a Certified Practising Valuer (CPV / API) and discuss negotiation with a licensed buyer's or selling agent.
